scenario: tmpfs mounted at /srv/quota-tmpfs with only grpquota_block_hardlimit=1m (no quota/usrquota/grpquota flag) — the contract's tmpfs '_hardlimit' clause must classify it enabled/enforced.

fixture.mountinfo:
29 29 0:24 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/nvme0n1p3 rw,errors=remount-ro
65 29 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:2 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@home
244 29 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
30 29 0:25 / /dev/shm rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:9 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,inode64
36 29 0:27 / /srv/quota-tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw,inode64,grpquota_block_hardlimit=1048576

rationale: Contract §C2 quota-classification table, tmpfs rows: 'tmpfs | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit | enabled | enforced | tmpfs_quota_option' and 'tmpfs | none of them | disabled | n/a | tmpfs_quota_options_absent'. The chosen mount's super options (last mountinfo field, proc.rst §3.5 field (m+4)) are 'rw,inode64,grpquota_block_hardlimit=1048576'. Its only quota-related key is 'grpquota_block_hardlimit', which is not one of {quota,usrquota,grpquota} but does end with '_hardlimit', so the first tmpfs row applies: quota_state=enabled, enforcement=enforced, basis=tmpfs_quota_option. Mount resolution (contract §C2 'Mount resolution'): realpath '/srv/quota-tmpfs' equals the mount point of the tmpfs line, which is the longest covering mount point; '/', '/home', '/tmp' and '/dev/shm' do not cover it, so fstype=tmpfs and mount_point=/srv/quota-tmpfs. Device check: fstype is not btrfs and the path's st_dev '0:27' equals the line's major:minor '0:27', so no 'device_mismatch' basis is substituted. Verdict precedence: one path is enabled, so exit=1 and finding_id=QUOTA_ENABLED (a positive finding is not hidden by any unknown sibling; there are no sibling paths). The value is written as the byte count 1048576, not the mount-time spelling '1m', because the kernel parses the limit with memparse and prints the parsed byte value, so '1m' never appears in mountinfo; the contract's key-only parsing (key = text before '=') makes the value immaterial to the classification. Sources: S084 Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst — quota mount-option table ('quota: User and group quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', 'grpquota: Group quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', 'grpquota_block_hardlimit: Set global group quota block hard limit') and 'Quota limit parameters accept a suffix k, m or g for kilo, mega and giga'; S082 Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst §3.5 — mountinfo field layout, field (6) mount options, optional fields up to the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and field (m+4) super options. Caveat recorded for the seal (not a change to this expectation): against a real v7.2 kernel this fixture's super-options state is not producible by a hardlimit-only mount, because the kernel copies the parsed limits into the superblock only when quota accounting was enabled on the mount, so a hardlimit key in mountinfo is always accompanied by usrquota and/or grpquota; the expectation above is the contract's rule applied to the contract's premise, and the same rule is what the oracle must implement.
